title: Quenched Gooey Turkish Herring Kazandibi
description: A resinous, gooey Turkish dish featuring herring, slow-cooked to perfection. Egg-free and friendly for those looking for a unique breakfast option.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine herring fillets, milk, sugar, cornstarch, and a pinch of salt. Whisk until the cornstarch dissolves.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let it cool slightly.
Add the unsalted butter, vanilla extract, black pepper, cinnamon, and nutmeg to the saucepan. Whisk until the butter melts and the mixture is smooth.
Strain the mixture into a clean saucepan, discarding the solids.
Return the mixture to the stovetop and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the water, rose water, and pistachio kernels. Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let the mixture cool slightly.
Pour the quenched mixture into individual serving dishes or a large serving dish. Let it set at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Serve chilled or at room temperature, garnished with additional pistachio kernels if desired.
Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
When serving, use a sharp knife to cut the quenched mixture into wedges or rectangles.
